semin-durr:26-26.t: The majority read «العظيم» in the genitive (jarr), following «الجلالة» [Translator's note: so in the text; in the genitive reading «العظيم» grammatically follows «العرش», as the rest of the entry indicates]. Ibn Muḥayṣin read it in the nominative (rafʿ). This admits two possibilities: that it is a naʿt (adjective) of «الرب», or that it is cut off (maqṭūʿ) from following «العرش» into the nominative, by implying an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject).

semin-durr:27-27.t: His saying: {أَصَدَقْتَ أَمْ كُنتَ}: the interrogative clause is in the position of the accusative (naṣb) by «نَنْظُرُ», because it is suspended (muʿallaqa) from operating on it. «أم» here is the connected (muttaṣila) one. His saying {أَمْ كُنتَ مِنَ الكاذبين} is more eloquent than saying «أم كَذَبْتَ», even though that is the basic form; because the meaning is: of those who are characterised by lying and have been strung on the thread of the liars.

semin-durr:28-28.t:
His saying: {هذا}: it may be a ṣifa (adjective) of «كتابي», or a badal (substitute) from it, or a bayān (explication) of it.

His saying: {فَأَلْقِهْ}: Abū ʿAmr, Ḥamza and Abū Bakr read it with the hāʾ unvowelled (sukūn); Qālūn with it in the kasra only, without lengthening (ṣila), with no disagreement transmitted from him. Hishām has two ways: shortening (qaṣr) and lengthening (ṣila). The rest read it with ṣila, with no disagreement. The justification of all this has already been given in Āl ʿImrān, al-Nisāʾ and elsewhere, at {يُؤَدِّهِ إِلَيْكَ} [Āl ʿImrān: 75] and {نُوَلِّهِ مَا تولى} [al-Nisāʾ: 115]. Muslim ibn Jundab read it with the hāʾ in the ḍamma, joined to a wāw: «فَأَلْقِهُوْ إليهم»; and it has already been stated that the ḍamma is the original.

[His saying:] «ثم تَوَلَّ عنهم»: Abū ʿAlī and others claimed that there is a fronting (taqdīm) in the speech, and that the original is: «فانظرْ ماذا يَرْجِعون ثم تَوَلَّ عنهم». There is no need for this, [because the meaning is sound without it, i.e.: stand close to them so that you may see what happens].

His saying: {مَاذَا يَرْجِعُونَ}: if we take «انظر» in the sense of "reflect and think", «ما» is interrogative, and it then has two aspects. The first: that it is made, together with «ذا», like a single noun, and is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of «يَرْجِعُون», the implied meaning being: "what thing do they return?" The second: that «ما» is made a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «ذا» is in the sense of «الذي», with «يَرْجِعُون» its ṣila (relative clause), and its returning pronoun omitted, the implied form being: "what thing is that which they return?" This relative noun is the khabar (predicate) of interrogative «ما». On both readings the interrogative clause is suspended from «انْظُرْ», so its position is the accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e.: "look into such-and-such and think about it". If, however, we take it in the sense of "wait", as in His saying {انظرونا نَقْتَبِسْ مِن نُّورِكُمْ} [al-Ḥadīd: 13], then «ماذا» is in the sense of «الذي», «يَرْجِعون» is its ṣila, and the returning pronoun is implied as has been established. This relative noun is a mafʿūl bihi, i.e.: "wait for that which they return".

The Shaykh [Translator's note: Abū Ḥayyān] said: "As for «ماذا»: if the meaning of «انظر» is reflection by thought, then «انظر» is suspended. «ماذا» is either an interrogative in the position of the accusative, or «ما» is interrogative and «ذا» a relative noun in the sense of «الذي». On the first, «يَرْجِعون» is a khabar of «ماذا»; on the second, «ذا» is the khabar, and «يَرْجِعُون» is the ṣila." End of quotation.

This is a mistake, either from the copyist or from someone else. That is because his saying "on the first" — by which he means that «ماذا» as a whole is an interrogative in the position of the accusative — precludes his saying that «يَرْجِعون» is a khabar of «ماذا». How can it be a khabar of it when it is what puts it in the accusative, as has been established? He himself stated explicitly that it is in the accusative — meaning by what follows it — and that what precedes it does not govern it. This is parallel to what preceded at the end of the previous sura, in His saying {وَسَيَعْلَمْ الذين ظلموا أَيَّ مُنقَلَبٍ يَنقَلِبُونَ} [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 227], in that the interrogative noun is governed by what follows it and suspends what precedes it. So just as you judged the clause made up of «يَنْقَلِبُوْن», together with the interrogative noun it contains and governs, to be in the accusative by way of suspension (taʿlīq), likewise you judge «يَرْجِعُون»; so how can you say that it is a khabar of «ماذا»?

semin-durr:30-30.t:
His saying: {إِنَّهُ مِن سُلَيْمَانَ وَإِنَّهُ}: the majority read both hamzas with kasra, as a resumption (istiʾnāf), in answer to a question from her people, as though they had said: "From whom is the letter? And what is in it?" So she answered them with the two answers.

ʿAbd Allāh [Translator's note: Ibn Masʿūd] read «وإنَّه مِنْ سليمانَ», adding a conjunctive wāw, conjoining «إنه من سليمان» to His saying {إني أُلْقِيَ إِلَيَّ}. ʿIkrima and Ibn Abī ʿAbla read both hamzas with fatḥa; al-Zamakhsharī and others stated this explicitly, while Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned only the kasra in «إنه من سليمان», and it seems he was silent about the second because it is conjoined to the first. In accounting for the fatḥa in both there are several aspects. The first: that it is a badal (substitute) from «كتاب» — a badal of inclusion (ishtimāl), or a badal of the whole for the whole — as though it were said: "There has been delivered to me that it is from Solomon, and that it is such-and-such." This is the soundest. The second: that it is nominative (marfūʿ) by «كريمٌ»; Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned it, and it is not strong. The third: that it is by dropping the particle of cause. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is permissible that you intend: because it is from Solomon, and because it…; as though she gave as the cause of its nobility its being from Solomon and its beginning with the name of Allah."

Makkī said: "Al-Farrāʾ permitted the fatḥa in both in [ordinary] speech"; as though he was not aware that it is a reading.

Ubayy read «أَنْ مِنْ سليمانَ، وأنْ بسمِ اللهِ», with the nūn unvowelled in both. There are two aspects in this; the more evident is that it is the explicative «أنْ» (al-mufassira), because something in the sense of "saying" precedes it. The second: that it is the lightened (mukhaffafa) one, with its noun omitted. This does not work on the principles of the Basrans, because its noun can only be the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), and the pronoun of the matter is explained only by a clause with both its parts stated explicitly.

semin-durr:31-31.t:
His saying: {أَلاَّ تَعْلُواْ}: there are several aspects in it. The first: that «أنْ» is explicative (mufassira), as was given among the aspects for the «أنْ» before it in the reading of ʿIkrima; al-Zamakhsharī mentioned nothing else. It is a good aspect because of the correspondence (mushākala) involved, namely the conjoining of the imperative to it, which is His saying «وَأْتُوْني». The second: that it is maṣdariyya (infinitival), in the position of the nominative as a badal (substitute) from «كتاب», as though it were said: "There has been delivered to me: that you not exalt yourselves over me." The third: that it is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e.: "it is that you not exalt yourselves." The fourth: that it is by removal of the preposition, i.e.: «بأَنْ لا تَعْلُوا», so the two well-known views about its position apply. What is apparent is that «لا» in these three aspects is that of prohibition. It has already been stated that maṣdariyya «أَنْ» may be joined to a fully inflected verb without restriction.

The Shaykh [Translator's note: Abū Ḥayyān] said: "«أنْ» in His saying «أن لا تَعْلُوا عليَّ» is in the position of the nominative as a badal from «كتاب». It has also been said: in the position of the accusative, [in the sense of]: «بأن لا تَعْلُوا». On these two readings «أنْ» puts the verb in the subjunctive (nāṣiba)." I say: the apparent sense of this is that it [Translator's note: i.e. «لا»] is negating, since it is inconceivable that it be prohibitive after the «أَنْ» that puts the imperfect in the subjunctive. This is supported by what he related from al-Zamakhsharī, for he said: "Al-Zamakhsharī said: «أنْ» in «أَنْ لا تَعْلُوا» is explicative." He said: "On this, «لا» in «لا تَعْلُوا» is for prohibition, and it is good because of the correspondence of conjoining the imperative to it." So his saying "on this…" to the end is explicit that on anything other than this — meaning the two preceding aspects — it is not for prohibition. Further, the view that it is for negation is not apparent, since the meaning would become a report from him (peace be upon him) that they do not exalt themselves over him; and that is not what is intended; what is intended is only that he forbids them from that.

Ibn ʿAbbās and al-ʿUqaylī read «تَغْلُوا», with the dotted ghayn, from «الغُلُوّ», which is exceeding the limit.

semin-durr:33-33.t: His saying: {مَاذَا تَأْمُرِينَ}: «ماذا» is the second object of «تَأْمُرين», and the first is omitted, its implied form being: «تَأْمُرِيْنَنَا». The interrogative suspends [the verb of] looking, and its ruling is not hidden given what preceded it.

semin-durr:34-34.t: His saying: {وكذلك يَفْعَلُونَ}: i.e. "the like of that action they do". Is this clause part of her speech — which is the apparent sense — so that it is in the accusative by the verb of saying; or is it part of the speech of Allah the Exalted, so that it is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya), with no grammatical position, and parenthetical between her two statements?

semin-durr:35-35.t:
«الهَدِيَّة» (gift) is what is sent by way of honouring. It is a noun for the thing given; it may be a pure noun, or it may originally be a maṣdar (verbal noun) applied to the passive participle. It is not a regular (qiyāsī) maṣdar, because the verb from it is «أهدى», a quadriliteral, so the regular form of its maṣdar is «إهداء».

His saying: {فَنَاظِرَةٌ}: conjoined to «مُرْسِلَة». «بمَ» is attached to «يَرجِعُ». Al-Ḥawfī erred in making it attached to «ناظِرَةٌ», and this is not sound, because the interrogative noun has the right to the head of the sentence. «بمَ يَرْجِعُ» suspends «ناظِرَةٌ».

semin-durr:36-36.t:
His saying: {فَلَمَّا جَآءَ سُلَيْمَانَ}: i.e. "and when the messenger came"; He left it implied because her saying «مُرْسِلَةٌ» indicates it, since it entails a messenger. What is meant by it is the genus, not literally a single messenger, as shown by his addressing them in the plural in his saying «أتُمِدُّونَنِ» to the end. For that reason ʿAbd Allāh read «فلمَّا جْاؤُوا», and read «فارْجِعوا إليهم», taking account of the underlying [plurality] referred to.

His saying: {أَتُمِدُّونَني}: an interrogative of disapproval (inkār). Ḥamza read it with the nūn of the indicative assimilated (idghām) into the nūn of protection (nūn al-wiqāya). As for the yāʾ, he drops it in pause and keeps it in continuous reading, according to his rule for the supernumerary yāʾs (al-zawāʾid). The rest read it with two nūns, according to the original. As for the yāʾ, Nāfiʿ and Abū ʿAmr, like Ḥamza, keep it in continuous reading and drop it in pause; Ibn Kathīr keeps it in both states; and the rest drop it in both states. It is related from Nāfiʿ that he read it with a single nūn, so the three readings are complete, as in {تأمروني أَعْبُدُ} [al-Zumar: 64].

Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: what is the difference between your saying «أتُمِدُّونني بمال وأنا أَغْنى منكم» ("Do you supply me with wealth, while I am richer than you?") and saying it with the fāʾ? I say: if I say it with the wāw, I have made the one I address aware of my exceeding him in wealth, while he nonetheless supplies me with wealth. If I say it with the fāʾ, I have made him one to whom my state was hidden, and I am only now informing him of that by which I have no need of his supply; as though I were saying: I disapprove of what you have done, for I have no need of it. And on this pattern came His saying: {فَمَآ آتَانِي الله}." End of quotation. This distinction is open to question, since that is not understood from the mere wāw and fāʾ. Moreover, he did not answer the first question, namely: why did he turn from saying «وأنا أغنى منكم» to saying {فَمَآ آتَانِي الله}? Its answer is that he attributed the giving of wealth to Allah to make manifest His favour upon him; had he said «وأنا أغنى منكم», there would have been boasting in it without mention of Allah's favour upon him.

His saying: {بَلْ أَنتُمْ}: an iḍrāb (turning) of transition. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: what is the point of the iḍrāb? I say: when he disapproved of their supplying him and gave the reason for his disapproval, he turned from that to explaining the cause that drove them to it, namely that they know no cause of contentment except the worldly goods given to them as gifts, besides which they know nothing. «الهديّة» may be annexed to the giver and to the one given to, and here it admits both."

The Shaykh [Translator's note: Abū Ḥayyān] said: "Here it is annexed to the one given to, and this is the apparent sense. It may also be annexed to the giver, i.e.: rather you, with this gift of yours which you gave, rejoice with the joy of boasting." I say: how can he make this first one the apparent sense, when it is not transmitted that Solomon ﷺ [Translator's note: the source uses the formula «صلَّى الله عليه وسلَّم» for Solomon] sent them a gift in this situation, so that it could be annexed to them? Rather, what is decisive is its being annexed to the giver.

semin-durr:37-37.t:
His saying: {ارجع}: the apparent sense is that the pronoun refers to the messenger. ʿAbd Allāh's reading «ارْجِعُوا» has already been given. It has also been said: it refers to the hoopoe.

His saying: {لاَّ قِبَلَ}: a ṣifa (adjective) of «جُنودٍ». The meaning of «لا قِبَلَ» is "no capacity"; its literal sense is "no facing". The pronoun in «بها» refers to «جنود», because it is a broken plural, so it is treated like a single feminine, as in their saying: «الرجال وأَعْضادُها» ("the men and their supporters").

ʿAbd Allāh read «بهم», according to the original.

His saying: {وَهُمْ صَاغِرُونَ}: a second ḥāl (circumstantial). The apparent sense is that it is emphatic (muʾakkida), because «أَذِلَّة» suffices in its place. If it is said: his saying «فَلَنَأْتِيَنَّهم» and «لنُخْرِجَنَّهُمْ» is an oath, so it must come to pass — the answer is that it is suspended on a condition omitted because the meaning is understood, i.e.: "if they do not come to me in submission".

semin-durr:39-39.t:
His saying: {عِفْرِيتٌ}: the majority read it with kasra on the ʿayn and sukūn on the yāʾ, followed by a tāʾ with tanwīn in the nominative [Translator's note: the text has «مجبورة», apparently for «مجرورة» or a similar word; translated by the sense of the reading]. Abū Ḥaywa read it with fatḥa on the ʿayn. Abū Rajāʾ and Abū al-Sammāl — and it is also related from Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq — read «عِفْرِيَةٌ», with a yāʾ with fatḥa followed by the feminine tāʾ which turns into hāʾ in pause. They cited for this the saying of Dhū al-Rumma:

3570 - كأنه كوكبٌ في إِثْر عِفْرِيَةٍ ... مُصَوَّبٌ في سوادِ الليلِ مُنْقَضِبُ
(As though it were a star in pursuit of an ʿifriya, hurled down in the blackness of the night, darting.)

A group read «عِفْرٌ», dropping the yāʾ and the tāʾ. These are four dialectal forms, and it has been read with all of them. It has two further forms: «عَفارِيَة»; and [the tribes of] Ṭayyiʾ and Tamīm say «عفرى», with the feminine alif, like «ذكرى». Its derivation is from «العَفْر», which is dust; one says «عافَرَه فَعَفَرَه», i.e. he wrestled him and threw him, casting him into the «عَفْر», which is dust. It has also been said: from «العُفْر», which is strength. The «عِفْريت» among the jinn is the rebellious, wicked one. One says «عِفْريت نِفْريت», which is a rhyming echo (itbāʿ), like «شَيْطان لَيْطان» and «حَسَن بَسَن». It is used metaphorically for a fierce, unruly human; and because this metaphor is well known, it is described in the verse as being of the jinn, to distinguish it. Ibn Qutayba said: "«العِفْرية» is the one of firmly knit build." The «عِفْرِيَة» of the cock and the bustard is the plumage on their heads. «عفرنى» is used for the strong one, and «رجلٌ عِفِرّ», with doubled rāʾ, for intensiveness, like «شَرٌّ شِمِرٌّ».

semin-durr:40-40.t:
His saying: {أَنَاْ آتِيكَ}: it may be an imperfect verb, its pattern being «أفْعِلُ», like «أَضْرِبُ», the original being «أَأْتِيْك» with two hamzas, the second of which was changed into an alif. Or it may be an active participle, its pattern being «فاعِل», the alif being supernumerary and the hamza radical — the reverse of the first. Ḥamza read «آتِيْكَ» with imāla (inclination) in both places in this sura, with a disagreement transmitted from Khallād.

His saying: {طَرْفُكَ}: there are two aspects in it. The first: that it is the eyelid, by which the speed of the matter is expressed. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is the movement of your eyelids when you look, and it was put in the place of looking." The second: that it is in the sense of «المَطْروف», i.e. the thing you look at. The first is the apparent one, because «الطَّرْف» has been described as being "sent forth" in the saying [of the poet]:

3571 - وكنتَ متى أرسَلْتَ طرفَك رائداً ... لقلبِك يوماً أَتْعَبَتْكَ المناظِرُ
رأيتُ الذي لا كلُّه أنت قادِرٌ ... عليه ولا عَنْ بَعْضِه أنتَ صابرُ
(Whenever you send forth your glance one day as a scout for your heart, the sights weary you: you see that over the whole of which you have no power, and without part of which you cannot bear to be.)

His saying: {مُسْتَقِرّاً}: a ḥāl (circumstantial), because the seeing is visual. «عنده» is governed by it. It is not to be said: when an adverb (ẓarf) occurs as a ḥāl, what it is attached to must be omitted, so how is it mentioned here? — because «الاستقرار» here is not that unrestricted "being present"; rather, what is meant by it here is the fixed thing that does not / waver. Abū al-Baqāʾ said this. Ibn ʿAṭiyya made it the very governor of the adverb which ought to have been omitted, saying: "The governor of the adverb appears in His saying «مُسْتَقرًّا»; this is what is always implied with every adverb, and it comes here overt; there is nothing like it in the Book of Allah." What Abū al-Baqāʾ said is better. Besides, the unrestricted governor has appeared overtly in the saying [of the poet]:

3572 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... فأنتَ لدى بُحْبُوْحَةِ الهَوْنِ كائنُ
(…for you are, in the midst of abasement, existing.)

This was established thoroughly at the beginning of al-Fātiḥa, so be sure to turn to it.

His saying: {أَأَشْكُرُ}: it suspends «لِيَبْلُوَني», and «أم» is connected (muttaṣila); likewise His saying {نَنظُرْ أتهتدي أَمْ تَكُونُ مِنَ الذين لاَ يَهْتَدُونَ} [al-Naml: 41].

His saying: {وَمَن شَكَرَ} {وَمَن كَفَرَ}: «مَنْ» may be conditional, or a relative noun containing the sense of condition; for that reason the fāʾ entered the khabar (predicate). The apparent sense is that the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of the second condition, or the khabar of the relative, is His saying {فَإِنَّ رَبِّي غَنِيٌّ كَرِيمٌ}; and in that case there must be a pronoun referring to «مَنْ», its implied form being: "free of need of his thanks". It has also been said: the apodosis is omitted, its implied form being: "then his disbelief is only against himself", because its counterpart — His saying {فَإِنَّمَا يَشْكُرُ لِنَفْسِهِ} — indicates it.

semin-durr:41-41.t: His saying: {نَنظُرْ}: the majority read it in the jussive (jazm), as the response to the imperative before it. Abū Ḥaywa read it in the indicative (rafʿ), making it resumptive.

semin-durr:42-42.t:
His saying: {أَهَكَذَا}: the preposition separates the particle of alerting (tanbīh) from the demonstrative. The original is «أكهذا», i.e. "Is the like of this your throne?" That is not permitted with anything other than the kāf: if you said «أبهذا مَرَرْتَ» and «أَلِهذا فعلتَ», it would not be permitted to separate «ها» and «ذا» with the preposition, saying «أها بِذا مَرَرْتَ» and «أها لِذا فَعَلْتَ».

His saying: {وَأُوتِينَا العلم}: there are two aspects in it. The first: that it is part of Bilqīs's speech, and the pronoun in «قَبْلِها» refers to the miracle and the situation indicated by the context. The meaning is: "We were given knowledge of Solomon's prophethood before the appearance of this miracle", or "before this situation"; that is because of what she had seen before that of the affair of the hoopoe and the returning of the gift. The second: that it is part of the speech of Solomon and his followers, so the pronoun in «قَبْلِها» refers to Bilqīs.

semin-durr:43-43.t:
His saying: {وَصَدَّهَا مَا كَانَت تَّعْبُدُ}: there are three aspects concerning the fāʿil (agent) of «صَدَّ». The first: the pronoun of the Creator. The second: the pronoun of Solomon. On this, {مَا كَانَت تَّعْبُدُ} is accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e.: "Allah — or Solomon — turned her away from what she used to worship besides Allah"; al-Zamakhsharī said this, allowing it. This is open to question, inasmuch as dropping the preposition is a poetic licence (ḍarūra), as in the saying [of the poet]:

3573 - تَمُرُّون الديارَ ولم تَعُوْجُوا ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(You pass the dwellings and do not turn aside…)

Thus said the Shaykh [Translator's note: Abū Ḥayyān]. Many verses of this kind have already been given, so this one has a precedent in them. The third: that the fāʿil is «ما كَانَتْ», i.e. "what she used to worship turned her away from Islam"; and this is clear. The apparent sense is that the clause «وصَدَّها» is conjoined to His saying «وأُوْتِيْنا». It has also been said: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from His saying «أم تكونَ من الذينَ», with «قد» implied; this is very far-fetched. It has also been said: it is resumptive, a report from Allah the Exalted of that.

His saying: «إنَّها»: the majority read it with kasra, as resumption and giving a reason. Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and Abū Ḥaywa read it with fatḥa, and there are two aspects in this. The first: that it is a badal (substitute) from «ما كانَتْ تعبدُ», i.e. "and her being [of a disbelieving people] turned her away". The second: that it is by dropping the particle of cause, i.e. «لأنَّها», so it is close to the reading of the majority.

semin-durr:44-44.t:
His saying: {الصرح}: the disagreement has already been given about the adverbial noun occurring after «دخل»: is it accusative as a ẓarf (adverbial), this being anomalous with «دخل» specifically, as Sībawayh said; or is it a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), like «هَدَمْتُ البيتَ», as al-Akhfash said? «الصَّرْح» is a palace, or the courtyard of a house, or a pavement made of glass. Its origin is from «التصريح», which is uncovering. «كَذِبٌ صُراحٌ» means a lie that is evident and exposed; likewise «لُؤْمٌ صُراحٌ» (open baseness). «الصَّريح» (the explicit) is the counterpart of «الكناية» (the allusive), because it is evident while its opposite is concealed. It has also been said: «الصريح» is the pure, from their saying «لَبَنٌ صَريحٌ» (pure milk), "clear in its «صَراحة» and «صُرُوحة»".

Al-Rāghib said: "«الصَّرْح» is a lofty, ornamented building; it was so called in consideration of its being clear of / admixture, i.e. pure."

His saying: {سَاقَيْهَا}: the majority read it with a plain alif. Qunbul related it with a hamza from Ibn Kathīr, and Abū ʿAlī judged it weak. Qunbul did the same in the plural of «ساق» in Ṣād and in al-Fatḥ, putting a hamza for its wāw; he read «بالسُّؤْقِ والأَعْناق» and «فاستوى على سُؤْقِه», with a hamza in place of the wāw. Another way is related from him: «السُّؤُوْق» and «سُؤُوْقه», with an added wāw after the hamza.

It is also related from him that he used to put a hamza in it in the singular, in His saying {يُكْشَفُ عَن سَأْقٍ} [al-Qalam: 42].

As for putting a hamza for the wāw, there are several aspects. The first: that an unvowelled wāw preceded by a ḍamma is turned into a hamza by some Arabs. This was established at the beginning of al-Baqara at «يُوْقنون», and I cited for it:

3574 - أَحَبُّ المُؤْقِدِين إليَّ موسى ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(The dearest of fire-kindlers to me is Mūsā…)

Abū Ḥayya al-Numayrī used to put a hamza for every wāw in the Quran having this description. The second: that «ساق» is on the pattern «فَعَل», like «أَسَد», so it was given the plural «فُعُل», with ḍamma on the ʿayn, like «أُسُد»; and a wāw with ḍamma is changed into a hamza, as in «وُجوه» and «وُقِّتَتْ»; then after being made a hamza it was made unvowelled. The third: that the singular is heard with a hamza, as will be established, so its plural came on that pattern.

As for «سُؤُوْق», with a wāw after the hamza: «ساق» was given the plural «سُوُوق», with [two] wāws, and the first was given a hamza because of its ḍamma. This transmission is rare (gharīb) from Qunbul, and we have read with it, praise be to Allah.

As for «سَأْقَيْها», the justification of the hamza is one of several aspects: either the dialect of those who change the alif into a hamza — on which is the usage of al-ʿAjjāj in «العَأْلَم» and «الخَأْتَم»; he recited:

3575 - وخِنْدِفٌ هامَةُ هذا العَأْلَمِ ...
(And Khindif is the head of this world…)

— and this will also be established at «مِنْسَأَته» in Sabaʾ, if Allah the Exalted wills, and part of it was given in al-Fātiḥa; or by likening it to «رَأْس» and «كَأْس», just as they said «حَلأْت السَّويق», by analogy with «حَلأُتُه عن الماء», i.e. "I drove him away"; or by treating the singular and the dual like their plural, and the hamza has been established in their plural.

His saying: {مُّمَرَّدٌ}: i.e. made smooth. From it is «الأَمْرَد» (beardless youth), for the smoothness of his face from hair; «بَرِّيَّة مَرْدَاء» (a bare wilderness), for its being devoid of vegetation; and «رَمْلَةٌ مَرْداء», sand that grows nothing. «المارِد» among the devils is one who is stripped bare of good and divested of it. «مارِد» is a well-known fortress. Among the proverbs of al-Zabbāʾ: «تَمَرَّد مارِدٌ وعَزَّ الأَبْلَقُ» (Mārid rebelled and al-Ablaq proved impregnable); she said it about two fortresses whose conquest was denied her.

«القوارِيْر» is the plural of «قارُوْرة», which is transparent glass. «مِنْ قواريرَ» is a second ṣifa (adjective) of «صَرْحٌ».

His saying: {مَعَ سُلَيْمَانَ}: attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl (circumstantial); it is not attached to «أَسْلَمْتُ», because his submission preceded hers by a long time. This is a subtle aspect. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "«مع» is an adverb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa; as for when the ʿayn is unvowelled, there is no disagreement that it is a particle." I say: the discussion of that has already been given. Makkī said here something similar to what Ibn ʿAṭiyya said.

semin-durr:45-45.t:
His saying: {أَنِ اعبدوا}: «أَنْ» may be explicative (mufassira), or maṣdariyya (infinitival), i.e. «بأَنْ اعْبُدوا»; then the two views about its position apply.

His saying: {فَإِذَا هُمْ فَرِيقَانِ}: the discussion of the «إذا» of surprise (al-fujāʾiyya) has already been given. What is meant by the two parties is the people of Ṣāliḥ, who split into two parties: believer and disbeliever. He stated this explicitly in al-Aʿrāf, where the Exalted said: {الذين استكبروا مِن قَوْمِهِ لِلَّذِينَ استضعفوا لِمَنْ آمَنَ} [al-Aʿrāf: 75]. Al-Zamakhsharī made the one party Ṣāliḥ alone and the other all his people. What led him to that is the conjoining with the fāʾ, for it signals that they became two parties as soon as he was sent, whereas his people would not become two parties except after some time, however short. «يَخْتَصمون» is a ṣifa (adjective) of «فريقان», as in His saying {هذان خَصْمَانِ اختصموا} and {وَإِن طَآئِفَتَانِ مِنَ المؤمنين اقتتلوا}. Regard for the plural [sense] was chosen here because it is a verse-ending (fāṣila).

semin-durr:47-47.t:
It has been read «تَطَيَّرْنا بك», which is the original, and [in «اطَّيَّرْنا»] it was assimilated. Its account has already been given.

His saying: {تُفْتَنُونَ}: it came in the second person out of regard for the preceding pronoun. Had what follows been regarded, it would have been said «يُفْتَنُون», with the yāʾ of the third person; that is permissible, but less preferred. You say «أنت رجلٌ تَفْعل» and «يَفْعل», with tāʾ and yāʾ, and «نحن قومٌ نقرأ» and «يَقْرؤون».

semin-durr:48-48.t:
His saying: {تِسْعَةُ رَهْطٍ}: most commonly the tamyīz (specification) of a number with this [word] is put in the genitive by «مِنْ», as in His saying {أَرْبَعَةً مِّنَ الطير} [al-Baqara: 260]. There are several positions on the question. The first: that it is permitted only rarely. The second: that it is permitted, but is not taken as a basis for analogy. The third: distinguishing between its / being for a small number, like «رَهْط» and «نَفَر», in which case it is permitted; or for a large number only, or for both large and small, in which case it is not permitted, as in «تسعةُ قوم». Sībawayh stated explicitly that «ثلاث غنم» is not allowed. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The specification of 'nine' by «الرَّهْط» was permitted only because it has the meaning of a plural, as though it were said: «تسعةُ أنفسٍ» (nine souls)." The Shaykh [Translator's note: Abū Ḥayyān] said: "The implied form given by others, «تسعة رجالٍ» (nine men), is better, because inasmuch as he annexed it to «أَنْفُس», he ought to have said «تِسْع أنفس», treating «النفس» as feminine, since the most eloquent usage treats it as feminine. Do you not see that they counted as anomalous the poet's saying:

3576 - ثلاثةُ أَنْفسٍ وثلاثُ ذَوْدٍ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Three souls and three camels…)"

I say: he only intended to explain the meaning.

His saying: {يُفْسِدُونَ}: it may be a naʿt (adjective) of the thing counted or of the number, so it is in the position of the genitive or of the nominative.

His saying: {وَلاَ يُصْلِحُونَ}: it has been said: it is emphatic of the first. It has also been said: it is not emphatic, because some corrupters may do good at some time; so He reported of these that even the supposition of that is negated.

semin-durr:49-49.t:
His saying: {تَقَاسَمُواْ}: «تقاسموا» may be an imperative, i.e. some of them said to others: "Swear to such-and-such." It may also be a past verb, and in that case it may be explicative of «قالوا», as though it were asked: "What did they say?" and the answer was: "They swore to one another." It may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial), with «قد» implied, i.e. "they said that, swearing to one another." Al-Zamakhsharī went this way, for he said: "It may be an imperative, or a report (khabar) in the position of a ḥāl with «قد» implied." The Shaykh [Translator's note: Abū Ḥayyān] said: "As for his saying 'or a report', it is not sound, because the report (khabar) is one of the two divisions of speech, since speech divides into report and performative (inshāʾ), and all its meanings, when examined, go back to these two divisions." I say: I do not know from what the unsoundness arises. For he made the past verb a "report" because it admits truth and falsehood, in contrast to the imperative, which does not admit them. As for speech dividing only into report and performative, and its meanings, when examined, going back to these two — what bearing has this on refuting Abū al-Qāsim [Translator's note: al-Zamakhsharī]? Then the Shaykh said: "Restricting by the ḥāl belongs only to the category of the relation of restriction, not to the relation of speech, which is predication (isnād). So when 'report' is applied to it, that is on the supposition that, had it not been a ḥāl, it could have been used as a report. Likewise their saying about a clause occurring as a ṣila (relative clause) that it is 'reportive' (khabariyya) is a figure of speech, the meaning being that, had it not been a ṣila, it could have been used as a report. There is obscurity in this." I say: it is granted that the clause, as long as it is a ḥāl or a ṣila, is not called "reportive" — meaning that it independently conveys predication — because it has been brought in the manner of a restriction in the case of the ḥāl, and in the manner of part of a word in the case of the ṣila. The clause occurring as a ṣifa (adjective) should also have been mentioned, for its ruling is the same.

Then he said: "As for implying «قد», there is no need for it, because the past verb occurs so frequently as a ḥāl without «قد» — with a frequency on which analogy ought to be based." I say: al-Zamakhsharī went along with the majority, for their position is that «قد» is indispensable, overt or implied, to bring it close to the present.

Ibn Abī Laylā read «تَقَسَّموا», without an alif, with the sīn doubled. «التقاسُم» and «التَّقَسُّم» are like «التظاهُر» and «التظَهُّر».

His saying: {بالله}: if you make «تقاسَمُوا» an imperative, the preposition phrase is attached to it, by unanimous view. If you make it a past verb, it may be attached to it, and then it does not fall under what is said, what is said being «لَنُبَيِّتَنَّه» to the end. It may also be attached to an omitted element, namely the verb of swearing, whose response is «لَنُبَيِّتَنَّه»; on this, it falls, together with what follows it, under what is said.

His saying: {لَنُبَيِّتَنَّهُ}: the two brothers [Translator's note: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] read it with the tāʾ of the second person with ḍamma, and ḍamma on the [final] tāʾ; the rest with the nūn of the speaker and fatḥa on the tāʾ. «ثم لَنَقولَنَّ»: the two brothers read it with the tāʾ of the second person with fatḥa and ḍamma on the lām; the rest with the nūn of the speaker and fatḥa on the lām.

Mujāhid, Ibn Waththāb and al-Aʿmash read like the two brothers, except with the yāʾ of the third person in both verbs. Ḥumayd ibn Qays read like this reading in the first, and like the reading of the Seven other than the two brothers in the second.

As for the reading of the two brothers: if we make «تقاسَمُوا» an imperative, the second person is clear, the end of the speech returning to its beginning. If we make it past, the second person is a recounting of their addressing one another with that. As for the reading of the rest of the Seven: whether we make it past or imperative, the matter in it is clear, namely the recounting / of their statements about themselves. As for the reading with the third person in both, it is evident if «تَقاسَمُوا» is past, the end of the speech returning to its beginning in the third person. If we make it an imperative, «لَنُبيِّتَنَّه» is an answer to an implied question, as though it were asked: "How did they swear?" and it was said: "[that] they would surely attack him by night". As for the third person in the first and the first person in the second, its justification is taken from what preceded in justifying the two readings.

Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«لَنُبيِّتَنَّه» has been read with yāʾ, tāʾ and nūn. With the tāʾ and the nūn, both aspects are sound in «تقاسَموا»" — meaning it is sound for «تقاسَمُوا» to be an imperative or a report. He said: "With the yāʾ, it can only be a report." I say: it is not so, because of what has preceded: that it may be an imperative, with the third person in what follows being the answer to an implied question. Abū al-Baqāʾ followed al-Zamakhsharī in this, saying: "«تقاسَمُوا» has two aspects. The first: it is an imperative, i.e. some of them ordered others to do that. On this, the nūn is permitted in «لَنُبَيِّتَنَّه», its implied form being: 'Say: we will surely attack him by night'; and the tāʾ, as the one ordering addressing the one ordered; but the yāʾ is not permitted. The second: it is a past verb, and on this the three aspects are permitted" — meaning by aspects the nūn, the tāʾ and the yāʾ. He said: "On this it is an explication" — i.e. «تقاسَمُوا», as a past verb, is explicative of «قالوا» itself. Makkī preceded them both in that. The justification of what they disallowed has already been given, and to Allah belong praise and grace. Fitting these aspects onto one another is something hard to extract from the words of the scholars; I have only arranged it from scattered statements. The discussion of {مَهْلِكَ أَهْلِهِ} has already been given in al-Naml [Translator's note: so in the text; this is al-Naml itself — the earlier discussion is presumably at «مَهْلِك» in al-Kahf 18:59].

semin-durr:51-51.t:
His saying: {أَنَّا دَمَّرْنَاهُمْ}: the Kufans read it with fatḥa, and the rest with kasra. The fatḥa has several aspects. The first: that it is by omission of the preposition, i.e. «لأَنَّا دَمَّرْناهم»; «كان» is complete (tāmma), «عاقبةٌ» is its fāʿil (agent), and «كيف» is a ḥāl (circumstantial). The second: that it is a badal (substitute) from «عاقبة», i.e. "how was our destroying them", in the sense of "how did it happen". The third: that it is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. «هي أنَّا دَمَّرْناهم», i.e. "the outcome is our destroying them". With these three aspects «كان» may also be deficient (nāqiṣa), with «كيف» made its khabar, so the aspects become six: three with «كان» complete and three with it deficient. With the deficient one, a further aspect is added: that «عاقبة» be made its noun, «أنَّا دَمْرناهم» its khabar, and «كيف» a ḥāl. These are seven aspects.

The eighth: that «كان» is redundant (zāʾida), «عاقبة» a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is «كيف», and «أنَّا دَمَّرْناهم» a badal from «عاقبة», or the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ; there is strain in this. The ninth: that it is also by omission of the preposition, except that it is the bāʾ, i.e. «بأنَّا دمَّرْناهم»; Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned it, and it is not strong. The tenth: that it is a badal from «كيف»; this is an error on the part of whoever said it, because with a badal from an interrogative noun the interrogative particle must be repeated, as in «كم مالكُ أعشرون أم ثلاثون؟» ("How much is your wealth — twenty or thirty?"). Makkī said: "In [ordinary] speech «عاقبة» may be put in the accusative, and «أنَّا دمَّرْناهم» made the noun of «كان»." End of quotation. Rather, this would be the preferable option, just as the accusative was preferable in His saying «فما كان جوابَ قومه إلاَّ أَنْ قالوا» and the like, because of what preceded about its resemblance to the pronoun, through being interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun). This has already been established.

Ubayy read «أَنْ دَمَّرْناهم»; this is the maṣdariyya «أَنْ» which can put the imperfect in the subjunctive, and what is said about it is like what is said about «أنَّا دَمَّرْناهم». As for the reading of the rest, it is by way of resumption (istiʾnāf), and it is an explication of the outcome. «كان» may be complete, deficient or redundant. «كيف» and what is in its domain are in the position of the accusative by removal of the preposition, because it suspends [the verb of] looking.

«أَجْمعين» is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the conjoined and what it is conjoined to together.

semin-durr:52-52.t: His saying: {خَاوِيَةً}: the majority read it in the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), its governor being the meaning of the demonstrative. ʿĪsā read «خاويةٌ» in the nominative: either as the khabar (predicate) of «تلك», with «بيوتُهم» a badal (substitute) from «تلك»; or as a second khabar, with «بيوتُهم» the first khabar; or as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. «هي خاويةٌ» — this is an implication that is dispensable. {بِمَا ظلموا} is attached to «خاوية», / i.e. because of their wrongdoing.

semin-durr:54-54.t:
His saying: {وَلُوطاً}: it is accusative either by conjunction with «صالحاً», i.e. "and We sent Lot"; or by conjunction with «الذين آمنوا», i.e. "and We saved Lot"; or by an implied «اذْكُرْ» ("mention").

His saying: {إِذْ قَالَ}: a badal (substitute) of inclusion (ishtimāl) from «لوطاً». Its parallel has already been given in Maryam and elsewhere.

semin-durr:55-55.t: His saying: {شَهْوَةً}: a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), or in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial); this has been given before.

semin-durr:56-56.t: His saying: {فَمَا كَانَ جَوَابَ قَوْمِهِ}: a fronted khabar (predicate) [of «كان»], and «إلاَّ أْن قالوا» is in the position of the noun [of «كان»]. Al-Ḥasan and Ibn Abī Isḥāq read it in the nominative as the noun, with «إلاَّ أنْ قالوا» as the khabar; this is weak, for reasons you have learned more than once. The two readings [Translator's note: the text has «قرآناً», apparently for «قراءتا»] of «قَدَّرْنا», with the dāl doubled and single, have already been given.

semin-durr:58-58.t: The specific object of blame (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is omitted, i.e. "evil was the rain of those warned — their rain."

semin-durr:59-59.t:
His saying: {قُلِ الحمد لِلَّهِ}: the majority read the lām of «قُلِ» with kasra, because of the meeting of two unvowelled letters. Abū al-Sammāl read it with fatḥa, for lightness; likewise in His saying {وَقُلِ الحمد للَّهِ سَيُرِيكُمْ آيَاتِهِ} [al-Naml: 93]. «سلامٌ» is a mubtadaʾ (subject); what permitted beginning with it [though indefinite] is its being a supplication.

His saying: «أَمْ ما»: this «أم» is the connected (muttaṣila), conjunctive one, since its conditions are fulfilled. The implied meaning is: "Which of the two is better?" «خيرٌ» is either an elative, in spite of the disbelievers and to bind the opponent [by his own premise], or an adjective with no comparison in it. «ما» in «أَمْ ما» is in the sense of «الذي»; it has also been said: it is maṣdariyya, and that is with the omission of a muḍāf from the first, i.e. "Is the affirmation of Allah's oneness better, or their associating partners?"

Abū ʿAmr and ʿĀṣim read «أَمْ ما يُشْرِكون», in the third person, by analogy with what precedes it in His saying. . . . [Translator's note: the text breaks off here in the source.]

semin-durr:60-60.t:
His saying: {أَمْ مَنْ خَلَقَ}: this «أم» is the disconnected (munqaṭiʿa) one, since neither an interrogative hamza nor [a hamza of] equivalence (taswiya) precedes it. «مَنْ خَلَقَ» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate) is omitted. Al-Zamakhsharī supplied it as «خيرٌ أَمْ ما تُشْرِكُون» ("better, or what you associate?"), supplying what was stated in the first interrogative; and this is good. Ibn ʿAṭiyya supplied it as: "His favour is denied and partners are associated with Him — and the like of this in meaning."

Abū al-Faḍl al-Rāzī said: "An equivalent clause must be implied, and that implied element has become like what is uttered, because the drift of the speech indicates it. The implied form of that clause is: 'Is He who created the heavens and the earth like one who did not create?' — and likewise its sister [verses]. He has made explicit elsewhere what He implied here, as in the saying of the Exalted: {أَفَمَن يَخْلُقُ كَمَن لاَّ يَخْلُقُ} [al-Naḥl: 17]." The Shaykh [Translator's note: Abū Ḥayyān] said: "Calling this implied element a 'clause' (jumla): if he means by it a group of words, that is sound; if he means the clause as technically defined in grammar, it is not sound; rather, it is an implied element of the single-word (mufrad) type."

Al-Aʿmash read «أمَنْ», with the mīm undoubled, making it the relative «مَنْ», with the interrogative hamza prefixed to it. There are two aspects in this. The first: that it is a mubtadaʾ with its khabar omitted, the implied form being as in the aspects given before; the Shaykh mentioned nothing else. The second: that it is a badal (substitute) from «الله», as though it were said: "Is He who created the heavens and the earth better, or what you associate?" Al-Zamakhsharī mentioned nothing else. In that case the badal is separated from what it substitutes by the khabar and by what is conjoined to the substituted noun. It is parallel to your saying «أزيدٌ خيرٌ أم عمروٌ أأخوك» ("Is Zayd better, or ʿAmr — your brother?"), with «أَأخوك» a badal from «أزيد»; and the permissibility of the like of this is open to question.

His saying: {فَأَنبَتْنَا}: this is a shift (iltifāt) from the third person to the first person, to emphasise the meaning of the act being exclusive to His Essence, and as a warning that making gardens of differing colours and tastes grow, while watering them with one water, is something none but He alone is capable of. For that reason He reinforced it with His saying: {مَّا كَانَ لَكُمْ أَن تُنبِتُواْ شَجَرَهَا}.

«الحَدائِق» is the plural of «حديقة», which is an orchard; it has also been said: a plot of land possessing water. Al-Rāghib said: "They were so called by likening them to the pupil (ḥadaqa) of the eye in shape and in water being present in it." Others said: they were so called because walls surround (iḥdāq) them; this is nothing, because the term is applied to them even without walls.

The readers paused on «ذات» in «ذاتَ بَهْجة» with a tāʾ [Translator's note: the text has «مجبورة», apparently for «مجرورة» or «مبسوطة», i.e. written open]; al-Kisāʾī with a hāʾ, because it is a feminine tāʾ.

His saying: {مَّا كَانَ لَكُمْ أَن تُنبِتُواْ}: «أن تُنْبِتُوا» is the noun / of «كان», and «لكم» is a fronted khabar. The negated clause may be a ṣifa (adjective) of «حدائق», or a ḥāl (circumstantial), since it [Translator's note: «حدائق»] has been specified by the adjective. Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «ذواتَ بَهَجة», in the plural, with fatḥa on the hāʾ of «بَهَجة».

semin-durr:61-61.t:
His saying: {خِلاَلَهَآ}: it may be an adverb (ẓarf) of «جَعَلَ» in the sense of «خَلَقَ» (create), which is transitive to one object; or it may be in the position of the second object, taking it in the sense of «صَيَّر» (make into).

His saying: {بَيْنَ البحرين}: what is permitted in «خلالَها» is permitted in it. «الحاجز» is the separator: «حَجَزَ بينَهم يَحْجِزُ», i.e. he prevented and separated.

«أَإِلَهٌ» has been read with both hamzas fully pronounced (taḥqīq), and with the second lightened, and with an alif inserted between them, with lightening and with easing (tashīl). All of this is known from the beginning of this topic. «أإلهاً» has been read in the accusative, by implying «أَتَدْعُوْنَ» ("do you call upon") or «أَتُشْرِكون» ("do you associate") a god.

semin-durr:62-62.t: «المُضْطَرّ» (the one in dire need) is a passive participle, taken from «اضْطُرَّ», which is used only in the passive. The "making" (al-jaʿl) was repeated here, and the objects were not made to share one governor, only because each one of these is an independent [favour] from Him, so He made it pass in a clause standing independently by itself.

semin-durr:63-63.t: His saying: {بُشْرَاً}: this has been given in al-Aʿrāf.

semin-durr:65-65.t:
His saying: {إِلاَّ الله}: there are several aspects in it. The first: that it is the fāʿil (agent) of «يَعْلَمُ», with «مَنْ» its object, and «الغيبَ» a badal (substitute) from «مَنْ السماواتِ» [Translator's note: so in the text, i.e. from «مَنْ في السماوات»], i.e. "none knows the unseen of those in the heavens and the earth except Allah", i.e. the hidden things that occur in the world. This is a strange aspect, mentioned by the Shaykh [Translator's note: Abū Ḥayyān]. The second: that it is a connected excepted (mustathnā muttaṣil) from «مَنْ»; but on this aspect one must combine the literal and the figurative in a single word, in the sense that His knowledge is in the heavens and the earth, so He is included in {مَن فِي السماوات والأرض} by this consideration, which is figurative, while others of His creatures in the heavens and the earth are [in them] literally. By that interpreted inclusion He is excepted from «مَنْ»; and the nominative as a badal is preferable because the speech is not affirmative.

Al-Zamakhsharī rejected this on the ground that it combines the literal and the figurative, and held that it must be disconnected (munqaṭiʿ). He said: "If you ask: why is the name of Allah in the nominative, when Allah is too exalted to be among those in the heavens and the earth? I say: it came according to the dialect of Banū Tamīm, where they say «ما في الدار أحدٌ إلاَّ حمارٌ» ('There is no one in the house except a donkey'), meaning: there is nothing in it except a donkey, as though «أحد» had not been mentioned. From this is the saying [of the poet]:

3577 - عَشِيَّةَ ما تُغْني الرِّماحُ مكانَها ... ولا النَّبْلُ إلاَّ المَشْرَفِيُّ المُصَمِّمُ
(On the evening when neither the spears avail in their place nor the arrows — only the Mashrafī sword that cuts through.)

and their saying «ما أتاني زيدٌ إلاَّ عمروٌ» ('Zayd did not come to me, only ʿAmr') and «ما أعانني إخوانكم إلاَّ إخوانُه» ('your brothers did not help me, only his brothers'). If you ask: what calls for choosing the Tamīmī usage over the Ḥijāzī? I say: a subtle, hidden point calls for it, in that the excepted is brought out in the manner of his saying:

3578 - إلاَّ اليَعافِيرُ. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ...
(…except the young gazelles…)

after his saying:

3579 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . لَيْسَ بها أنيسُ ...
(…in which there is no companion…)

so that the meaning comes down to your saying: if Allah is among those in the heavens and the earth, then they know the unseen" — meaning: their knowing the unseen is as impossible as Allah's being one of them; just as the meaning of what is in the verse is: if the young gazelles are companions, then there is a companion in it — a decisive assertion that it is empty of companions. "If you ask: why do you not claim that Allah is among those in the heavens and the earth, as the theologians say 'Allah is in every place', in the sense that His knowledge is in all places, so it is as though His Essence were in them — so that it need not be taken according to the usage of Banū Tamīm? I say: what precludes that is that His being in the heavens and the earth is figurative while their being in them is literal, and for a speaker to intend by a single expression both the literal and the figurative is not sound. Besides, your saying 'those in the heavens and the earth', and your bringing Him together with them under the application of a single name, carries a suggestion of equating [them], and such suggestions are to be removed from Him and His attributes. Do you not see how he (peace be upon him) said to the one who said 'and whoever disobeys them both has gone astray': 'What a bad speaker for the people you are!'?" I say: so he preferred the disconnection, and excused his adopting the Tamīmī usage by what he mentioned. Most scholars hold that the literal and the figurative are not combined in a single word; al-Shāfiʿī held that it is.

His saying: {أَيَّانَ}: here it is in the sense of «متى» (when), / and it is accusative by «يُبْعَثون», [and the interrogative] suspends «يَشْعُرون» [Translator's note: the text has «فتعلُّقُه», apparently for «فتُعَلِّقُ»], so it, together with what follows it, is in the position of the accusative by dropping the bāʾ, i.e. "they do not perceive such-and-such". Al-Sulamī read «إيَّان», with kasra on the hamza; it is the dialect of his tribe, Banū Sulaym.

semin-durr:66-66.t:
His saying: {ادارك}: Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr and Nāfiʿ read «أَدْرَكَ», like «أَكْرم». The rest of the Seven read «ادَّارك», with a connecting hamza (hamzat al-waṣl), the dāl doubled with fatḥa, followed by an alif. The original is «تَدارك», and Ubayy read it so. The tāʾ was to be assimilated into the dāl, so it was changed into a dāl and made unvowelled; beginning with it then became impossible because of its sukūn, so the connecting hamza was brought in, and it became «ادَّارك» as you see. The detailed account of this has been given at the head of the ḥizb in al-Baqara: {فادارأتم فِيهَا} [al-Baqara: 72]. As for the reading of Ibn Kathīr, it has been said: «أَفْعَلَ» in it may be in the sense of «تَفاعَلَ», so the two readings coincide. It has also been said: «أَدْرَكَ» is in the sense of "reached and came to an end". Sulaymān and ʿAṭāʾ, the two sons of Yasār, read «بلَ ادَّرَكَ», with fatḥa on the lām of «بل» and the dāl doubled, without an alif after it. Its explanation is that the original is «ادَّرك» on the pattern «افْتَعَل»; the tāʾ of «افتعال» was changed into a dāl because it occurs after the dāl. The Shaykh [Translator's note: Abū Ḥayyān] said: "So there occurred in it the conversion of the second to the first, as in their saying «اثَّرَدَ», whose original is «اثْتَرَدَ», from «الثَّرْد»." End of quotation. I say: this is not one of the cases where the second is converted to the first for the sake of assimilation, like «اثَّرَدَ» from «اثْتَرَدَ»; because the tāʾ of «افتعال» is changed into a dāl after certain letters, among them the dāl, as in «ادَّان», «افْتَعَل» from «الدَّيْن»; so the change is because the dāl is the first radical (fāʾ), not for assimilation; so it is not like «اثَّرَدَ» in any way. Reflect on it, for it is fine. Then when the dāl was assimilated into the dāl, the interrogative hamza was prefixed, so the connecting hamza dropped, and the word became «أَدْرَكَ» with a disjunctive hamza (hamzat al-qaṭʿ) with fatḥa; then the vowel of this hamza was transferred to the lām of «بل», so the word became «بَلَ دَّرَكَ».

Abū Rajāʾ, Shayba, al-Aʿmash, al-Aʿraj and Ibn ʿAbbās read likewise — and it is also related from ʿĀṣim — except with kasra on the lām of «بل», according to the rule for the meeting of two unvowelled letters, since they did not bring an interrogative hamza.

ʿAbd Allāh, Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḥasan and Ibn Muḥayṣin read «أادْرَكَ», with a hamza followed by an alif. Its original is two hamzas, the second of which was changed into an alif for lightness. Abū ʿAmr disapproved of it. I say: it was given at the beginning of al-Baqara that «أَانْذَرْتَهم» has been read with a plain alif, so this one has a precedent in it. Abū Ḥātim said: "An interrogative is not permitted after «بل», because «بل» is affirmation, while the interrogative in this place is disapproval in the sense of 'it was not', as in the saying of the Exalted {أَشَهِدُواْ خَلْقَهُمْ} [al-Zukhruf: 19], i.e. they did not witness; so the two cannot occur together, because of the incompatibility between affirmation and disapproval." I say: disallowing this is open to question, because «بل» is for the iḍrāb (turning) of transition: he has turned away from the first speech and taken up a second interrogative. How can this be disapproved of, when the grammarians render disconnected «أم» by «بل» and the hamza? I wondered at the Shaykh, how he said here: "Some of the later scholars permitted the interrogative after «بل» and the like. A speaker says: «أخبزاً أكلْتَ، بل أماءً شرِبْتَ» ('Was it bread you ate? Rather, was it water you drank?'), leaving the first speech and taking up the second." End of quotation. His restricting it to some of the later scholars signals that the earlier scholars and some of the later ones disallow it; and it is not so, because of what I have related from them about disconnected «أم».

Ibn Masʿūd read «بل أَأَدْرَكَ», with both hamzas fully pronounced. Warsh, in one transmission, read «بلَ ادْرَكَ», with transfer [of the hamza's vowel] (naql). Ibn ʿAbbās also read «بلى ادْرَك», with the particle of affirmation, the sister of «نَعَم», and «بَلى آأَدْرك», with an alif between the two hamzas. Ubayy and Mujāhid read «أم» instead of «بل»; this contradicts the standard text (al-sawād).

His saying: {فِي الآخرة}: there are two aspects in it. The first: that «في» has its usual sense, and «أَدْرَك», though past in form, is future in meaning, because it will certainly come to pass, as in His saying {أتى أَمْرُ الله} [al-Naḥl: 1]; on this, «في» is attached to «ادَّاركَ». The second: that «في» is in the sense of the bāʾ, i.e. «بالآخرة»; on this, it is attached to "their knowledge" itself, as in your saying «عِلْمي بزيدٍ كذا» ("my knowledge of Zayd is such-and-such"). As for the reading of whoever read «بلى», al-Zamakhsharī said: "Since He brought «بلى» after His saying {وَمَا يَشْعُرُونَ}, its meaning was: 'Yes, they do perceive'; then He explained / the perceiving by His saying {أَدْرَكَ عِلْمُهُمْ فِي الآخرة}, by way of sarcasm, whose meaning is an emphatic negation of knowledge." Then he said: "As for the reading «بلى أَأَدْرك», as an interrogative, its meaning is: 'Yes, they perceive when they will be raised.' Then He disapproved of their [claimed] knowledge of its coming to be; and when He disapproved of their knowledge of its coming to be, no perception of the time of its coming to be can be attained by them, because knowledge of the time of an occurring thing follows knowledge of the occurring thing's coming to be." Then he said: "If you ask: what is the meaning of these three iḍrābs? I say: they are nothing but a stepping down through their states: He described them first as not perceiving the time of the resurrection, then as not knowing that the Resurrection will come to be, then as floundering in doubt and uncertainty." End of quotation.

If it is said: «عَمِيَ» is made transitive with «عن» — you say «عَمِيَ فلانٌ عن كذا» ("so-and-so was blind to such-and-such") — so why was it made transitive with «مِنْ» in His saying «مِنْها عَمُوْن»? The answer is that He made the Hereafter the starting point and source of their blindness.

semin-durr:67-67.t:
His saying: {أَإِذَا}: the discussion of the two interrogatives when they come together has been given in Sūrat al-Raʿd, with its detailed account. The governor of «إذا» is omitted, indicated by «لَمُخْرَجُون», its implied form being: «نُبْعَثُ ونَخْرُجُ» ("we will be raised and brought out"). «مُخْرَجُون» cannot govern it, because of three impediments: the interrogative, «إنَّ», and the lām of inception (lām al-ibtidāʾ) — and about the lām of inception in the khabar of «إنَّ» there is disagreement. Al-Zamakhsharī showed his cleverness here and put it in a sweet expression, saying: "Because before the active participle can govern it there are obstacles (ʿiqāb), namely the interrogative hamza, «إنَّ» and the lām of inception; one of them would suffice, so how much more when they all come together?" He also said: "If you ask: in this verse He put «هذا» before {نَحْنُ وَآبَآؤُنَا}, and in another verse He put {نَحْنُ وَآبَآؤُنَا} before «هذا»! I say: fronting is evidence that what is fronted is what is meant and relied upon in the mention, and that the speech was brought for its sake. So in one of the two verses it indicates that bringing about the resurrection is what the speech was aimed at, and in the other, bringing about the one resurrected, in that respect."

«آباؤُنا» [Translator's note: the text has «آباؤُها»] is conjoined to the noun of «كان»; the separation by the preposition phrase stood in place of separation by the emphatic [pronoun].

semin-durr:72-72.t:
His saying: {رَدِفَ لَكُم}: there are several aspects in it. The most evident: that «رَدِفَ» has been made to include (ḍummina) the sense of a verb made transitive with the lām, i.e. "drew near, came close, approached"; Ibn ʿAbbās explained it so. «بعضُ الذي» is its fāʿil (agent). It has also been made transitive with «مِنْ», on the basis of its including the sense of «دنا»; [the poet] said:

3580 - فلمَّا رَدِفْنا مِنْ عُمَيْرٍ وصَحْبِه ... توَلَّوْا سِراعاً والمنيَّةُ تُعْنِقُ
(When we drew close to ʿUmayr and his companions, they turned away swiftly, with death racing after.)

i.e. "we drew near to ʿUmayr". The second: that its object is omitted, and the lām is for cause, i.e. "the creation followed on because of you and your ill omen". The third: that the lām is added to the object for emphasis, as it is added in his saying:

3581 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... أَنَخْنا لِلكَلاكِلِ فارْتَمَيْنا
(…we made [the camels] kneel on their breasts, and we flung ourselves down.)

and like the addition of the bāʾ in the saying of the Exalted: {وَلاَ تُلْقُواْ بِأَيْدِيكُمْ} [al-Baqara: 195]. On these aspects the pause is on «تَسْتَعجلون». The fourth: that the fāʿil of «رَدِفَ» is the pronoun of the promise, i.e. "the promise followed on", i.e. what it entails came near and approached; «لكم» is a fronted khabar (predicate) and «بعضُ» a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject). On this the pause is on «رَدِفَ»; and this involves breaking up the speech. The fifth: that the verb is taken in terms of its maṣdar, i.e. «الرَّدافةُ لكم» ("the following-on is for you"), and «بعضُ» on the implied form «رَدافةِ بعضٍ», meaning so that the khabar and what it is predicated of correspond. This is weaker than what preceded it.

Al-Aʿraj read «رَدَفَ», with fatḥa on the dāl; it is a dialectal form, and the kasra is better known.

semin-durr:73-73.t: His saying: {لاَ يَشْكُرُونَ}: its object may be omitted, i.e. "they do not give thanks for His favours". It may also not be supplied at all, in the sense of "they do not acknowledge His favours"; so He expressed the absence of their recognition of the favour by the absence of what follows from recognising it, namely thanks.

semin-durr:74-74.t: His saying: {مَا تُكِنُّ}: the majority read the tāʾ of the imperfect with ḍamma, from «أَكَنَّ»; the Exalted said: {أَوْ أَكْنَنتُمْ} [al-Baqara: 235]. Ibn Muḥayṣin, Ibn al-Samayfaʿ and Ḥumayd read it with fatḥa on it [Translator's note: the text has «بتفحها», a slip for «بفتحها»] and ḍamma on the kāf. One says «كَنَنْتُه» and «أكْنَنْتُه», in the sense of "I hid and concealed".

semin-durr:75-75.t: His saying: {وَمَا مِنْ غَآئِبَةٍ}: there are two views about this tāʾ. The first: that it is for intensiveness, as in «راوِيَة» and «عَلاَّمة». The second: that it is like the tāʾ that enters maṣdars (verbal nouns), as in «العاقِبَة» and «العافِيَة». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Parallel to them are «الذَّبيحة», «النَّطيحة» and «الرَّمْيَة», in that they are nouns, not adjectives."

semin-durr:78-78.t: His saying: {بِحُكْمِهِ}: the majority read it with ḍamma on the ḥāʾ and sukūn on the kāf. Janāḥ ibn Ḥubaysh read it with kasra on it and fatḥa on the kāf, as the plural of «حِكْمة».

semin-durr:80-80.t: His saying: {وَلاَ تُسْمِعُ الصم الدعآء}: its detailed treatment has been given in al-Anbiyāʾ (peace be upon them).

semin-durr:81-81.t:
His saying: {بِهَادِي العمي}: the majority / read «هادِيْ», annexed to «العُمْي». Ḥamza read «يَهْدِي», an imperfect verb, with «العمُيَ» in the accusative as the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); likewise the one in al-Rūm. Yaḥyā ibn al-Ḥārith and Abū Ḥaywa read «بهاد», with tanwīn, with «العُمْيَ» in the accusative by it; and this is the original.

The readers agreed on pausing on «هاد» in this sura with the yāʾ, because it was written in the muṣḥaf with it present. They differed in al-Rūm: the two brothers [Translator's note: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] also paused on it with the yāʾ, as here. As for Ḥamza, it is because he reads it «يَهْدي», an imperfect verb in the indicative, so its yāʾ is retained. Al-Kisāʾī said: "Whoever reads «يَهْدِي» is bound to pause with the yāʾ." He is bound to that only because the verb does not take a tanwīn in continuous reading for whose sake the yāʾ is dropped, so that it would be likewise in pause — as a tanwīn enters «هادٍ» and the like, so the yāʾ goes in continuous reading, and the pause follows that, like one who pauses without the yāʾ. End of quotation. It follows from that that one should pause on {يَقْضِي بالحق} [Ghāfir: 20] and {وَيَدْعُ الإنسان} [al-Isrāʾ: 11] keeping the yāʾ and the wāw. But Ḥamza is bound [only] to depart from the written form, not from analogy. As for al-Kisāʾī, he reads «بهادي» as an active participle like the majority; so his keeping the yāʾ is by analogy with «هادِي» in this sura, and in it there is a departure from the written form of the early generations (al-rasm al-salafī).

His saying: {عَن ضَلالَتِهِمْ}: there are two aspects in it. The first: that it is attached to «يَهْدي», and it was made transitive with «عن» because it includes the sense of "turns them away". The second: that it is attached to «العُمْي», because you say «عَمِيَ عن كذا» ("he was blind to such-and-such"); Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned it.

semin-durr:82-82.t:
His saying: {وَإِذَا وَقَعَ القول}: i.e. the content of the word; or the maṣdar (verbal noun) was applied to the object, i.e. "what is said".

His saying: {تُكَلِّمُهُمْ}: the majority read it with doubling. There are two aspects in it. The more evident: that it is from speech and talk; this is supported by the reading of Ubayy «تُنَبِّئُهم» ("informs them") and the reading of Yaḥyā ibn Sallām «تُحَدِّثُهم» ("talks to them"), both of which are explanations of it. The second: "wounds them"; this is indicated by the reading of Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn Jubayr, Mujāhid, Abū Zurʿa and al-Jaḥdarī, «تَكْلُمُهم», with fatḥa on the tāʾ, sukūn on the kāf and ḍamma on the lām, from «الكَلْم», which is wounding. «تَجْرَحُهم» has also been read. In the exegesis [it is stated] that it brands the disbeliever.

His saying: {أَنَّ الناس}: the Kufans read it with fatḥa, the rest with kasra. As for the fatḥa, it is by implying the bāʾ, i.e. «بأنَّ الناسَ»; this is indicated by its being stated explicitly in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh, «بأنَّ الناسَ». This bāʾ may then be for transitivity, or causal. On both readings, «تُكَلِّمهم» may have either of its two senses, talking and wounding, i.e. "it tells them that mankind…", or "because mankind…"; or "it wounds them with 'that mankind…'", i.e. brands them with these words, or brands them because of the absence of faith.

As for the kasra, it is by way of resumption. It may then be part of the speech of Allah the Exalted — which is the apparent sense — or part of the speech of the Beast; but then «بآياتنا» ("Our signs") troubles it. This is answered either by its special connection [with Allah], which makes it sound to annex the signs to it, as the followers of kings say "our mounts and our horses" when they belong to their king; or by omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "the signs of our Lord". If «تُكَلِّمهم» is from talk, then [the kasra] may be either by treating «تُكَلِّمُهم» like «تقولُ لهم» ("says to them"), or by implying the verb of saying, i.e. "and it says such-and-such"; and this saying is an explanation of «تُكَلِّمُهم».

semin-durr:83-83.t: His saying: {مِن كُلِّ أُمَّةٍ}: it may be attached to the gathering, with «مِنْ» for the beginning of the extent; or attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «فَوْجاً», because it may originally have been a ṣifa (adjective) of it. «الفَوْج» is a group, like «القوم». Al-Rāghib restricted them, saying: "the group passing by in haste"; and it seems this is the original, and then it was applied generally, even where there is no passing by or haste. The plural is «أفواج» and «فُؤُوج». «مِمَّنْ يُكَذِّبُ» is a ṣifa of it. «مِنْ» in «مِنْ كلِّ» is partitive, and in «مِمَّن يُكَّذِّبُ» explicative (tabyīniyya).

semin-durr:84-84.t:
The wāw in «ولم تُحِيْطُوا» may be the conjunctive one, or the circumstantial (ḥāliyya) one. «عِلْماً» is a tamyīz (specification).

His saying: «أَمْ ماذا»: «أم» here is disconnected (munqaṭiʿa); its ruling has been given. «ماذا» may as a whole be an interrogative in the accusative by «تَعْمَلون», which occurs as the khabar (predicate) of «كنتم»; or «ما» may be an interrogative mubtadaʾ (subject), with «ذا» a relative noun as its khabar, the ṣila (relative clause) being «كنتمُ تعملون», with its returning pronoun omitted, i.e. "what thing is that which you used to do?"

Abū Ḥaywa read «أَمَا», with the mīm undoubled; he made the interrogative hamza enter upon its noun [Translator's note: i.e. the interrogative «ما»], for emphasis, as in his saying:

3582 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... أهَلْ رَأَوْنا بوادي القُفِّ ذي الأَكَمِ
(…Did they see us in the valley of al-Quff, the one with the hillocks?)

semin-durr:85-85.t: His saying: {بِمَا ظَلَمُواْ}: i.e. because of their wrongdoing. Making «ما» in the sense of «الذي» is weak.

semin-durr:86-86.t: His saying: {لِيَسْكُنُواْ فِيهِ}: it has been said: there has been omitted from the first what has its counterpart stated in the second, and from the second what has its counterpart stated in the first; since the implied meaning is: "We made the night dark / that they might rest in it, and the day giving sight that they might go about in it." So «مُظْلِماً» ("dark") was omitted because «مُبْصِراً» indicates it, and «لِيتصَرَّفوا» ("that they might go about") because «لَيَسْكُنُوا» indicates it. His saying «مُبْصِراً» is like His saying {آيَةَ النهار مُبْصِرَةً} [al-Isrāʾ: 12], and its detailed account has been given in al-Isrāʾ. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: why was the parallelism not observed in His saying «لِيَسْكُنوا» and «مُبْصِراً», since one of them is a cause and the other a ḥāl (circumstantial)? I say: it is observed in terms of meaning; and such is natural, unaffected composition."

semin-durr:87-87.t:
His saying: {فَفَزِعَ}: [in the past] rather than «فَيَفْزعُ», because of its certainty, as in His saying {رُّبَمَا يَوَدُّ الذين} [al-Ḥijr: 2] and {أتى أَمْرُ الله} [al-Naḥl: 1].

His saying: {أَتَوْهُ}: Ḥamza and Ḥafṣ read «أَتَوْه», a past verb, its object being the hāʾ. The rest read «آتُوْه», an active participle annexed to the hāʾ. This is construing by the meaning of «كُلّ», which is annexed by implication, i.e. «وكلَّهم» ("and all of them"). Qatāda read «أتاه», attributed to the pronoun of «كُل» according to its form; then he construed it by its meaning and read «داخِرين». Al-Ḥasan and al-Aʿraj read «دَخِرين», without an alif.

semin-durr:88-88.t:
His saying: {تَحْسَبُهَا جَامِدَةً}: this clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «ترى» or from its object, because the seeing is visual.

His saying: {وَهِيَ تَمُرُّ}: the clause is also a ḥāl. Thus it is with huge bodies: you see them standing still while they are passing. Al-Nābigha al-Jaʿdī said, describing a dense army:

3583 - بأَرْعَنَ مثلِ الطَّوْدِ تَحْسَبُ أنَّهم ... وُقوفٌ لِحاجٍ والرِّكابُ تُهَمْلِجُ
(With a huge host like a mountain; you would think they were halted for some need, while the mounts are pacing swiftly.)

«مرَّ السَّحابِ» is a maṣdar (verbal noun) of comparison.

His saying: {صُنْعَ الله}: a maṣdar emphasising the content of the preceding clause, its governor being implied, i.e. "Allah made that a making"; then it was annexed after its governor was omitted. Al-Zamakhsharī made it emphatic of the governor of {يَوْمَ يُنفَخُ فِي الصور} [al-Naml: 87], and supplied it as: "On the day the trumpet is blown, and such-and-such happens, Allah rewards the doers of good and punishes the doers of evil" — in a long passage, hovering around his school's doctrine. It has also been said: it is accusative by way of incitement (ighrāʾ), i.e. "Look at the making of Allah, and hold to it."

«الإِتْقان» (perfecting) is producing a thing in the most complete of its states. It is from their saying «تَقَّن أَرْضَه», when he drives water thick with mud to his land so that it becomes fit for cultivation. [One says] «أرضٌ تَقْنَةٌ». «التَّقْن» is doing that to it; and «التَّقْن» is also what is cast of that into the pool or onto the land.

His saying: {بِمَا تَفْعَلُونَ}: Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr and Hishām read it in the third person, following His saying «وكلٌّ أَتَوْهُ». The rest read it in the second person, following His saying «وتَرى», because what is meant is the Prophet ﷺ and his community.

semin-durr:89-89.t:
His saying: {فَلَهُ خَيْرٌ مِّنْهَا}: there are two aspects concerning «خيرٌ». The first: that it is for comparison (tafḍīl), with regard to their claim, or with omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "better than its worth and what it deserves"; so «مِنْها» is in the position of the accusative. [The second:] that it is not for comparison, so «منها» is in the position of the nominative as a ṣifa (adjective) of it.

His saying: {مِّن فَزَعٍ يَوْمَئِذٍ}: the fatḥa and the genitive of «يوم» have been given in Hūd. «إذ» is annexed to a clause that has been omitted and replaced by the tanwīn. The best is to supply it as: "on the day when he comes with the good deed". It has also been said: "on the day when you see the mountains"; and it has been said: "on the day when the trumpet is blown". The first is preferable because what is supplied from is near.

semin-durr:90-90.t: His saying: {هَلْ تُجْزَوْنَ}: by implying a verb of saying; and this saying is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from what precedes it, i.e. "their faces were thrown down, that saying being said to them".

semin-durr:91-91.t: His saying: {الذي حَرَّمَهَا}: this is the reading of the majority, as a ṣifa (adjective) of «الرَّب». Ibn Masʿūd and Ibn ʿAbbās read «التي», as a ṣifa of «البلدة». The context concerns the Lord, not the city; for that reason the majority reading is clear.

semin-durr:92-92.t:
His saying: {وَأَنْ أَتْلُوَ القرآن}: the majority read it with the wāw retained after the lām. There are two interpretations of it. The first, which is the apparent one: that it is from «التلاوة», which is recitation, and what follows suits it. The second: from «التُّلُوّ», which is following, as in His saying {واتبع مَا يوحى إِلَيْكَ} [Yūnus: 109]. ʿAbd Allāh read «أنْ اتْلُ», as an imperative to him (peace be upon him); so «أن» may be the explicative one (mufassira), or the maṣdariyya one joined to an imperative; what there is to say about this has been given.

His saying: {وَمَن ضَلَّ}: the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) may be His saying {فَقُلْ إِنَّمَآ}, and then there must be an omitted pronoun referring to the conditional noun, i.e. "of those who warn him", for the reason given in al-Baqara. Or the apodosis may be omitted, i.e. "then the evil consequence of his going astray is upon him".

semin-durr:93-93.t: His saying: {عَمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ}: it has been given at the end of Hūd that it has been read with yāʾ and with tāʾ.

semin-durr:1-1.t:
His saying: {وَكِتَابٍ}: The majority read it in the genitive, conjoined to «القرآن». Is what is meant the Qurʾān itself, so that it is a case of conjoining one attribute to another with one referent; or the Preserved Tablet; or the sūra itself? It is also said: al-Qurʾān and al-Kitāb are both proper names for what was sent down upon our Prophet Muḥammad ﷺ, so they are like al-ʿAbbās and ʿAbbās; meaning that the al- in both is for evoking the attribute. This is a mistake, for if they were both proper names they would not be described by an indefinite, but «قرآن» was described by it in His saying {تِلْكَ آيَاتُ الكتاب وَقُرْآنٍ مُّبِينٍ} [verse 1] in Sūrat al-Ḥijr, and «كتاب» was described by it as in this noble verse. What is said is that it is indefinite here to convey magnification, as in His saying the Exalted {فِي مَقْعَدِ صِدْقٍ} [al-Qamar: 55].
Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «كتابٌ مبينٌ» with both in the nominative, conjoined to «آياتُ», which is predicated of «تلك». If it is asked: how is it sound to point at two, one of them feminine and the other masculine, with the demonstrative of the feminine, whereas if you said «تلك هندٌ وزيدٌ» it would not be permissible? The answer has three aspects. The first: that what is meant by the Book is the verses, because the Book is an expression for verses gathered together; so since they are one thing, / pointing at both with the demonstrative of the feminine singular is sound. The second: that there is an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "and the verses of a clear Book". The third: that when the feminine is followed by what it is correct to point to it with, that suffices and is good; had the masculine followed it, it would not be good. Do you not see that you say «جاءَتْني هندٌ وزيدٌ», and if you omitted «هند» or postponed it, the feminine form of the verb would not be allowed?

semin-durr:2-2.t: His saying: {هُدًى وبشرى}: Several possibilities are allowed for both. The first: that they are both accusative as maṣdars of an implied verb from their own words, i.e. "it guides with guidance and gives good news with good news". The second: that they are both in the position of ḥāl from «آياتُ», the governor in it being the meaning of pointing in «تلك». The third: that they are both in the position of ḥāl from «القرآن»; there is weakness in this because it is a muḍāf ilayhi. The fourth: that it is a ḥāl from «كتاب» in the reading of one who made it nominative; it is weak in the reading of one who made it genitive, because of what preceded, that it is in the status of the muḍāf ilayhi through being conjoined to it. The fifth: that they are two ḥāls from the latent pronoun in «مبين», whether you make it nominative or genitive. The sixth: that they are two badals from «آيات». The seventh: that they are a khabar after a khabar. The eighth: that they are two khabars of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "they are guidance and good news".

semin-durr:3-3.t:
His saying: {الذين يُقِيمُونَ}: It may be in the genitive position as a naʿt of «للمؤمنين», or a badal, or a bayān; or accusative for praise; or nominative by implying a mubtadaʾ, i.e. "they are those who".
His saying: {وَهُم بالآخرة هُمْ يُوقِنُونَ}: The second «هم» is a repetition of the first by way of verbal emphasis (tawkīd lafẓī). Al-Zamakhsharī understood restriction (ḥaṣr) from it, i.e. none have certainty of the Hereafter in its true sense except those described with these attributes. And «بالآخرةِ» is attached to «يُوقنون», and the separation between them by the emphasis does no harm. This clause may be conjoined to the ṣila, entering within the scope of the relative; in that case he has varied the two ṣilas for a reason: since establishing prayer and paying zakāh are things that recur and renew, he brought both ṣilas as verbal clauses, saying «يُقيمون» and «يُؤْتُون». And since certainty of the Hereafter is an established matter whose continuance is demanded, he brought the ṣila as a nominal clause, with the subject repeated in it and the object of certainty fronted in it, which indicates specification, to indicate permanence and stability. And he brought the khabar of the mubtadaʾ in this clause as an imperfect verb, indicating that this is renewed at every time without interruption. It is also possible that it is resumptive, not within the scope of the relative.
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is possible that the ṣila is completed, in his view," i.e. at His saying «وهم». He said "and the clause is parenthetical (iʿtirāḍiyya)". He means that the ṣila is complete at «الزكاةِ», so it is possible in that way; otherwise how would it be sound, if we take his words at face value, that the ṣila is complete at His saying «وهم»? His calling this a parenthesis is in respect of meaning and the flow of the speech; otherwise the parenthetical in technical usage is what occurs between two mutually required elements, such as mubtadaʾ and khabar, condition and apodosis, oath and its response, follower and followed, ṣila and relative; and there is nothing of that here.

semin-durr:5-5.t:
His saying: {الأخسرون}: There are two views on afʿal here. The first, and it is the apparent one: it is in its ordinary sense of comparison (tafḍīl), with respect to the disbelievers, in view of the difference of time and place. Meaning: they are greater in loss in the Hereafter than they are in this world, i.e. their loss in the Hereafter is greater than their loss in this world. A group, among them al-Kirmānī, said: "It is here for intensification, not for sharing, because the believer has no loss at all in the Hereafter." The answer to that has already been covered: the loss refers to one thing, considered with the difference of its time and place.
Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "Al-akhsarūn is the plural of «أَخْسَر», because afʿal as an adjective is not pluralised unless annexed, whereupon its rank among nouns is strengthened; and in this there is something to consider." The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) said: "There is nothing to consider in that it is pluralised as a sound plural or a broken plural when it has al-; rather only that is allowed, when what precedes it agrees with it in plurality.
